speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Mr. Rodgers there to examine it, and yet conditions arose which no past experience enabled us to grapple with. There were difficulties in connection with the prosecution of the work which led to differences of opinion between the officers of the department and the contractors, which had to be settled in some way, and which it will be admitted, I think, were settled in as satisfactory a way as possible. Even a resort to courts would not, I think, be as satisfactory or as advisable.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Has the council approved of the award ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Not yet. It is still open. The stage to wihich the matter has progressed is this. The recommendation has been received from these gentlemen by the chief engineer, but it has not yet been followed up. It came in since the session opened, land we have not had time to enter into it.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Has the chief engineer of the department mentioned his opinion or pledged himself according to the recommendation of these three engineers ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Yes. It happened that they all three agreed.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Has the chief ei* gineer given his certificate yet ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: No.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: All I can say is that it is a most extraordinary proceeding. The Exchequer Court was formed for the purpose of settling these difficulties. By the contract the chief engineer is the judge as to the quantities and the work, and upon his certificate the amounts are paid. Then, a board of engineers is appointed, for what purpose ? To inform the chief engineer what he ought to know himself, and the other engineers on the work, and they recommend that he shall give a certificate for certain prices and certain quantities.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: There is no question about the quantities.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
The prices surely are fixed by the contract. There could be no difficulty at all with the chief engineer nor with the engineers in charge of the work, and I suppose there was not any. They certified as to the amount of work done. The contractor is not satisfied. In that ciase, there is a way of proceeding which we intended should be followed in all these cases, that is, to go to the Exchequer Court. But a convenient wav is adopted of referring the question to three arbitrators-for what purpose ? To provide a conscience for the chief engineer, to tell him wliat the prices and the quantities

are, and lie perforce has to follow their opinion and give his certificate in accordance with it. 1 hear tihat he has not given his certificate, and that the matter has not yet been before council. I hope that such an objectionable manner of proceeding will never receive the sanction of council, but that it will be sent back to the chief engineer for his certificate. If he has not certified to it, there must be a difference of opinion between the chief engineer and the contractors, or the contractors would not ask for a board of engineers to be appointed to look over the works and see what quantities are. The contractors must in some manner have received from the department the prices which the department chose to put on the work; and, if I understand the minister -properly, there is a difference in the prices, but not in the quantities. They knew the prices the department was putting on the work, and if there was any difference, there was only one right way of settling it, that was, to go to the Exchequer Court, which was formed for the purpose of deciding such cases.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
I can only siay that, from my experience in the department of the results of appeals to the Exchequer Court,
I cannot concur in the conclusion the hon. gentleman lias arrived at. The differences which arose were differences respecting the value of the work which these people did. My hon. friend said they should be governed by the -prices, which prices would of course lie stated in the contract. It does not happen that there were any prices in the contract for -the particular work which formed the subject-matter of this claim. The engineers and officers had not foreseen-and that is where the difficulty of this particular class of structure came in-the necessity which arose for many descriptions of work separate from the contract. These claims were claims for extras, and it was necessary and proper that the amount of allowance which could properly be made to these people should be settled in some way or other. It is not unknown to the hon. gentleman in his experience that questions of that kind constantly arise in the department, and you could not ask the chief engineer to act as an arbitrator as between these parties, so that they would feel that they had fair consideration. The chief engineer, having an opinion on the subject, as far as he could form an opinion in respect of it, would not be willing to act, and he has always uniformly since he lias been in the department declined to act in any such capacity. The hon. gentleman knows that right well. IJe says that in that alternative we could go to the Exchequer Court. Could anybody who wished to be fair and reasonable say that an Exchequer Court is an ideal tribunal for the purpose of ascertaining the value of the work that these people did ? Or would a better tribunal be a board of engineers in whom you are entitled to have confidence, men of high standing, and men who you know would give you the benefit of their very best judgment. As between man and man, which would any one say was the proper tribunal to go to ? I cannot think that there is any room for doubt. If anybody will say that Mr. Joseph Hobson or Mr. Robert Surtees, known as they are by everybody as reliable men as could be found in Canada, are not many times more competent to pass on a question of this kind than a judge of the Exchequer Court, then I will admit that we have gone the wrong way about bringing this matter to an end. You have to bring these matters to an end in some way; you cannot leave them hanging for ever. It is the duty of the minister in the department, and I intend to pursue that course while I am in the department, to have these claims disposed of as speedily as possible. There is no advantage in having men hanging around yo-u from time to time waiting to have this question or that question disposed of. You had better pay a little too much than have that condition of things. If it were my hon. friend's own business and he wanted to protect himself, he could uot pursue a wiser or more proper course, and he could pot select any men who would be worthier of public confidence in such a trust than the men we chose for the purpose.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAIRWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
What was the amount of* the original contract and by whom was the plan prepared ?
The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS You will get the total amount by taking the quantity. The original cou-tiact totals up $500,000 and the extras $120.000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
The contract is not finished yet.
The MINISTER ('I, RAILWAYS AND CANALS. This is an estimate based upon the schedule prices in the market.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I understand the minister to say that the contract is going on still and that this is an arbitration on progress estimates ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Yes, it will take some three or four weeks perhaps to finish.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
As I understand the case, the contract is not for a lump sum for the entire work, but an estimate was made that a certain quantity of walls and other work would be required, and a price was fixed of so much per yard for concrete work, labour and materials. These were all placed in a schedule. It seems to me that if plans and specifications were prepared, which showed a superstructure of a certain size, surely one could arrive at a lump sum for the contract, but instead there were

schedule prices fixed, and after the completion of the work and measuring up the entire structure, the amount due was to be arrived at. It does seem odd that on a contract involving approximately half a million dollars, the departmental engineer should be one-quarter out. The minister says that half a milion dollars was what the work was to cost.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: There was a change made in the work.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Which involved a cost of $129,000 more. There should have been no difficulty in arriving at a price to be paid for the extra work done. The minister had the benefit of the prices given in the original contract, and surely these would have furnished a basis for estimating the Extras. It does seem odd that before the extras were begun, a hard and fast bargain was not made with the contractors. When the extras were commenced was there any basis settled, showing how much per yard or otherwise these extras should cost, or any schedule prices agreed to ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
There was a material change made in the plan. [DOT] and in some other respects, and upon this change a claim was based. The handling of the material was made very much more expensive by reason of that change, and that is one of the items.
Hon. Mr. HA(30ART. Did the chief engineer certify as to the amount he thought these parties were entitled to ?
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: He had his views with regard to what would be a fair price.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Did he certify to that ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: 1 cannot say.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
Will the hon. gentleman ask his chief engineer, who is alongside of him ?
'Hit MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS. Pie certified to the progress estimates.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: There has not been a final estimate made out yet ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: No.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: This is $139,000 over what the chief engineer certified to, on progress estimates, that he thought the parties were entitled to.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: The hon. gentleman is going up a little. He lias increased the figure from $120,000 to $139,000.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: The hon. minister has not answered the question I put to him, which was this : Before the extras began, were any prices arrived at and submitted to the contractor ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: No, the chief engineer had his views of what was a fair price, but they were not satisfactory to the contractor, and lienee the difficulty.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
If I understand the minister aright the position was this. Here was a contract let by the department to a firm of contractors under schedule prices for the work to be done. No lump sum could be arrived at because it was not known what quantities of material would pass into (he work and what amount of labour would be required. But schedule prices were prepared and plans and specifications made out and the work began. At a certain stage the minister made up his mind to change the formation of the work to a certain ex-t(*nt, and the contractors were shown a plan of the changes contemplated and asked ti>
go on with the work. The minister had in his own mind an idea of what the prices should be for the extras, but the contractors refused to accept his figures. The minister then said to the contractors: You go on with the work and we will make a settlement afterwards. I think I have put the case fairly.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: You put it fairly enough if the facts were as you have stated them.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
I have put the facts as I understood the minister to have stated them. The extra work was contemplated by the minister. He will not deny that. He had information from his engineer as to what would he fair prices.
The MINISTER OF RAILWAiS AND CANALS. The difficulty had really arisen long before it first came to my knowledge. The work had been proceeded with, and I did rot know it. It is not many months ago when the matter was first brought to my attention. The progress estimates had been going on some time before, based on the ideas of the chief engineer. His ideas did not agree with those of the contractors, and they began to think it was time some agreement was reached. Then the question was put before me, and after talking the matter over witli the chief engineer. I agreed that these three men should arbitrate.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: A change was contemplated in the plan ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: It was actually made in the work.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
Is the House to understand that a change was made in the work

with tlie consent of the minister or that it was unknown to him until this claim was made ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I did not know about the change when it was made. I never knew anything about it until the question came up as to what would be a proper price.
speakername: The MINISTER OP RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
I did not understand the minister in that light Now we are in this position-here	is a contract
for work that will cost approximately half a million. While the work is progressing, the contractor, of his own accord, makes certain changes in the work, the minister knowing nothing whatever about them. After the contractor has performed the work in part he comes to the minister and says : I have made a lot of changes in the work and I demand from you payment for the extra work involved. And it seems that something in the neighbourhood of $125,000 is to be paid for work which the contractor alleges he did hut which is entirely unknown to the minister. Is that the position ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I was unaware personally of what, was being done. As I say the fii-st knowledge I had of any difference between the department and the contractors was when the matter was brought before me, as it were, on appeal between the chief engineer and the contractors. At the time the question first came up a number of engineers had been down there at the instance of Messrs. Corry & Laverdure for the purpose of estimating the character and the reasonable cost of the work. There were some five or six of these engineers, including Mr. Kennedy, of Montreal, Mr. Keefer, Mr. Jennings and a number of others whose names are quite familiar to ns all. These gentlemen had written their reports-not jointly-setting forth what they thought this character of work was worth. There was a very considerable difference of opinion between these engineers and the chief engineer of the department. We knew that if the matter went to the Exchequer Court that court would have no means of reaching a decision except by summoning engineers and taking their evidence under oath. Therefore we hit on the expedient of agreeing that engineers who had not previously been invited by Messrs Corry & Laverdure to look at the work and who had no connection with them should examine the work and give their opfnion to tjie chief engineer. This idea we carried out.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: For the better understanding of this matter will the hon. minister give the quantities of the work as originally left to Messrs Corry & Laverdure and then the change in the work with the quantities. The hon. minister must see that when extra work is performed by a contractor under the government and the engineers differ as to the prices or quantities -for the principle would apply to quantities also-they would have the same right as Messrs Corry & Laverdure to have an advisory hoard of engineers selected. I very much doubt that the chief engineer, having given his certificate of the value and quantity of the work, will change his certificate upon the recommendation of any set of engineers in the country. It is an extraordinary proceeding that, after giving his decision, he would revise it on the advice of other engineers. He is the chief engineer and ought to he as capable of forming an opinion as to prices and quantities as any board of advisory engineers can be. And. in view of just such disputes as the present one, this country formed a court to decide such matters, and when such cases arise, they ought to be sent to that court.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: As I understand the case, as developed by (the hon. member for Sim-eoe (Mr. Bennett) and the hon. Minister of Railways, 'these contractors performed certain work wholly unauthorized by the minister and without his knowledge. The question is, is the minister, under these circumstances, going to pay for the work 1 Is.be making these preparations with a view to paying for that work thus done without his authority ? If that can be done 'by one contractor there is no end to the expenditure that may be incurred in spite of the minister. Surely, there must he some control over public works. These gentlemen, according to the hon. minister's own statement, did work that he never authorized, yet the hon. gentleman is making every preparation to ascertain just what they ought to be paid for it. Surely the only way to deal with contractors who take this view of their position is to let them lie on the bed they have made-not pay them. Then, perhaps, they will keep within their contracts.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I would like to know the difference in quantities.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I beg the hon. gentleman's pardon, if he was expecting an answer tonight, I thought I said that we had not the information at hand and could not give it to him.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Then the hon. gentleman will give it to me some other time ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
Yes.
IICm. Mr. HAGGART. Is there any item on which this subject will come up again ?
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Certainly, we have supplementary estimates.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
I think we should have some explanation from the minister how it happened that the work for which a claim of $300,000 is made and for which

an award of $126,000 was made subsequently, could be done without the knowledge and authority of the minister.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I have no doubt the hon. gentleman (Mr. Haggart) who was in the department before me would have more experience than I in that direction. Many changes are made in these works. Either the chief engineer or the engineers under him by his authority may make these changes, which do not necessarily come to the personal knowledge of the minister.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: But the hon. gentleman did 'not state before that this was done on the authority of the chief engineer.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Undoubtedly, it was on the authority of the chief engineer. And no doubt, the contractors were fully authorized to do it. I have not the slightest recollection of any question at all arising with reference to the canal or the possibility of these claims coming up until they actually arose. My first knowledge of it was when the work had progressed and we were nearing the time when the final estimate had to be paid and the^question would have to be settled in one form or another.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: In view of that explanation, which I did not understand before, it is clear that the question of my hon. friend from Simcoe (Mr. Bennett) remains to be answered. He wanted to know, if these changes were made, why the scale of prices was not fixed af the time the changes were authorized, and the minister answered by saying they were not fixed because he did not know anything about it. That might be a very good answer if it were correct. It turns out now' it is not correct, because when we speak of the minister we speak of his department, of his officers.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I stated to the hon. gentleman that the chief engineer had his ideas then as to what would be proper prices at the time the changes were commenced, but the contractors notified him that the work could not be done at those prices. I think I said that, at all events I intended to say it.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Then the position of the matter is this, according to the minister's last statement. When these changes were contemplated a discussion ensued between the chief engineer and the contractors as to the extra wrork. Now, the minister has not stated whether this was simply a matter of conversation or a matter of record in the department. Can the minister tell us whether these negotiations on the part of the contractors to make these changes, and the statement made in turn by the chief engineer as to the prices which he thought fair, were these matters of record in the department ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I do not know what the hon. gentleman means by negotiations. There were not any until after the work had progressed. The chief engineer stated what he thought were proper prices, and he made his progress estimates and the amount of the estimates was accepted, and payments were made upon them. But the contractors protested from time to time that this work *was costing a good deal more than they were being allowred.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Then it was agreed upon between the contractors and the chief engineer that certain extra work was to be proceeded with.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: It was decided by the chief engineer that changes should be made.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Changes that are commonly called extras. Now when these extras were contemplated there was a difference of opinion between the engineer and the contractors. The engineer said what he thought would be a fair price for the work, that is to say in the gross amount at schedule prices. To that proposition there was demurrer on the part of the contractors, they not acquiescing in the prices proffered by the chief engineer. Now I ask the minister is that a correct statement of the facts ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I think that is substantially correct, as I am given to understand. Prices were named by the chief engineer, the contractors did not agree with those prices, and from time to time, as the work went on, and it was found what the work cost, the contractors protested, and protested, and protested again.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Then this whole matter of negotiation must either have been by discussion or conversation between the contractors and the engineer,' or by connected correspondence. Can the minister say which was the case ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: The chief engineer was not presented with a written protest; they verbally protested from time to time.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I am referring to the proffer of prices on the part of the department through the chief engineer, and the refusal of the contractors to accept such prices. Is that a matter of record ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: The matter of record is that the chief engineer made his progress estimates allowing certain prices in regard to the extras.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
That is after the work is done. You cannot make an estimate of progress until after the work is done. The question is, before they began these extras

did the department offer the contractors certain terms, certain prices for the extras that were contemplated, or did they not ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Yes, the chief engineer said : Now we propose to make this change and we propose to allow such and such prices.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Was this proposition in writing ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: No, it appeared in the estimates, the chief engineer said.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: The estimate cannot appear until the work is done. I am asking, when the proposition was made that they should do certain extras.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: They are progress estimates.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: But a progress estimate is not made until a certain amount of work is done. I am asking as to these extras, how were they done or entered upon ? Did the department propose that these extras should he done, alterations made in the work, and did they offer certain prices, and are those in writing ?	.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: The chief engineer says he thinks the first time the price appeared was when the first progress estimate was made.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Then the work was begun without authority ; the extra work must have been begnn without authority, if the first time it was brought up was when he was making an estimate for progress work already begun.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: They were authorized to go on and make these changes.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Is that on record in the department-anything to show the changes contemplated ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: They were instructed to make these changes as the chief engineer suggested, they were bound to make them.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: That is coming to the point. Now the point in this. The minister had decided upon certain changes in the ' work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: The department had.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Well, the department is the minister and the minister is the department. These changes being contemplated, without having any record at all or any agreement as to the price to be paid, these contractors went on with the work. Now is that a fair statement of the case ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
That would be a fair statement. They were instructed to go on with this
work, and there were no prices allowed until the first progress estimates came up.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Then may I ask the minister what was the nature of the extras ? Was it similar to the work under the original contract ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: No, it was not.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Then wherein did they differ ? In the changes that were made was there additional masonry work, or in what particular was the change ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I am told there was a large quantity of water-tight embankment required that was not provided for in the original contract ; that was in place of steel work.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: He must have had the written authority of the chief engineer for that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: He was instructed to do it.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: A contractor is not entitled to any extras unless he has the written authority of the chief engineer to make them. Further, when he does extra work beyond his contract, he has to notify the department within a certain number of days in* writing. If he does not do it, no matter what his extras are, he is not entitled to anything under the contract. He must first have the authority of the chief engineer to make any changes in the contract. No engineer on the contract has authority to do it. We ought to have the facts. The hon. minister has promised to furnish them afterwards. We should know what changes were made in the original contract and what the work which 'was authorized to be done by the chief engineer, together with the quantities and prices allowed.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: The hon. minister cannot ask to have this item passed without the information which is the whole basis of the discussion.

speechtext:
Certainly.
Soulanges canal, construction and equipment,
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

speechtext: What are the construction and equipment, and what sums are necessary ? lion. Mr. HAGGART. Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.

One hundred and eight thousand will be the amount that will be coming to them probably when the contract is completed.
Welland canal-Improvements at Port Col-borne entrance, $300,000.

speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

speechtext: How much was spent last year ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: $200,000. When I say last year, I mean the current year. We expect to speud $200,000 this year out of the vote of $300,000. We are revoting $100,000 and we are adding to that $200,000. We think that will complete the work.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.

speechtext: You nave no idea as to the proportion which the Public Works Department are doing ?

speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

speechtext: When do you expect to have it finished ?

speechtext: We will have our part finished just as soon as the breakwater is completed. It is not worth our while to push our portion of the work through before the breakwater is completed.

speechtext:
What is the nature of the work being done by the hon. gentleman's department at Port Colborne ?
Th.e MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS. We are widening the entrance and deepening it. Wre are erecting piers and extending the piers along the west side and we are erecting two docks so as to afford facilities for the docking of two steamers on each side.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I have* never been at Port Colborne so that I am not very conversant with the position of the harbour. Am I to understand that there is a dock on either side of the entrance ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: No, only on the west side. There is a short projecting pier on the east side. There is a long projecting pier on the west side, and at the end of that we are making arrangements for two docks on which elevators may be constructed.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Who is the contractor for this work ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Messrs Hogan & McDonald are our contractors.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: How much are . you going to lower the mitre sill at Port Colborne ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Three feet.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: What is the use of deepening the water on the mitre sill unless you deepen the reach.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
The mitre sill at the entrance only shows 13 feet and instead of lowering it so as to make sure of a clear 14 feet we have made it 1C feet, because of the effect

of the winds which makes the water shallower at the entrance. We do not propose to lower the other locks because they are able to afford 14 foot navigation, nor do we propose to make the channel 16 feet.
Kapide Plat-Canal.' $57,600.
The MINISTER OB' RAILWAYS AND CANALS. $32,600 of this is a revote.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
Who is working there.
The MINISTER OB'1 RAILWAYS AND CANALS. Gilbert Brothers.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
This is simply work to remove work that was done there by Mr. Broder the contractor under the plan of the present superintending engineer. I do not And fault with the present work, but I do say that it has been become necessary because of work which was done at great cost by the present superintending engineer. M e are spending this money to undo work that should never have been done in the first place.
The MINISTER OB" RAILWAYS AND CANALS. Do you mean that the work which is being taken oat was authorized by Mr. Rubidge.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Yres. There was a great deal of piering being done there and when it was being done the boatmen complained that the entrance could not be used, but notwithstanding that the engineer persisted in going on with the work and that work has now to be removed. The original work was done by Mr. Broder.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: The chief engineer believes that the work must have been done before he came into the department. He says that since he came in there was nothing- done by the Broders.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: That may be, but the original work was laid out by the present superintending engineer.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I am more concerned, and I suppose the Chief Engineer is also, as to the propriety of doing what we are now doing, and I understand from him that it is necessary that this work should be done.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
I think it is right too that this work should be done.
Galops canal, enlargement, $293,600.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: $55,000 of this is a re vote.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
I claim that the work that is being done in the Galops channel interferes with the entrance to the canal to a certain extent, because it draws tile water away from that. I have always taken the stand that that work in the Galops channel is an outrage, and I would
like to bring it to the attention of the minister and make an appeal to him to have it stopped. The work was advised and commenced a number of years ago by the present superintending engineer, and was carried on for a number of years. I think that in the neighbourhood of $1,000,000 has been paid to the contractors who have been working there since the hon. minister has had charge of the department. The work was originally started with a view to enabling large steamers to navigate the Galops rapids. Steamboat men from year to year appealed to the government, claiming that those people could never navigate those rapids, even if the channel was made 17 feet deep. At the same time they claimed that that deep cut through the rapids would lower the water in the St. Lawrence above the rapids. After eight or ten years work in the channel, it was said to be completed and fit for use. I complained myself to the government, and insisted on an investigation, and instead of there being 17 feet of water, it was proved that there was only some 10 feet. Previous to my complaint, it was proved to the satisfaction of the government that the channel would never be of any use, and the scheme of putting a lock below the rapids was entertained, and the work was completed, and that is now being used. Every marine man that I know of on the river will admit that every vessel will go through that lift lock and will never use the channel.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: There are occasionally vessels that go down.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
I live right there and see the rapids every day, and there are no steamers using that channel, unless a very small steamer which is more like a yacht. Even the old propellers, which are now out of date, all go through the canal. The hon. gentleman will find that no marine insurance commpany will take any risk on a steamer that will go down that channel. The firm that was working there last year, from the 1st of May to the 1st of December, were getting $425 a day. The minister said they only received $18,000 last year. That must be an error. They must have received $80,000 or $90,000 for last year's work, and it is currently reported that as soon as this session is over they are going to do it again. I wish to appeal" to the hon. minister, as I did before, to have this work stopped, because in the eyes of the people it looks like an outrage to see the money squandered in this way. I do not think the minister has looked into this matter as he should, or he would never allow that work to continue for one hour longer, because it is simply squandering the public money and making a present of $375 a day to that firm. They are not working every day, and you are paying them $425 a day, and they do not work 25 days in the season. Why should

this government pay $375 a day of clear profit to any firm in this country ? The people in my county would rather see you pay this firm a bonus of $30,000 or $40,000, rather than put it in this way, when they know that the whole thing is an imposition on the country. I would like the minister to let us know when this thing will be finished, so that it will be known that it is through, and no more money will be squandered on it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I think, from what I am told, that there is something due to these people for work done last year, and I am advised that there will be a sum placed in the supplementary estimates, not a large sum. for the work-not for the purpose of making any new excavation, or taking out any new rock, but simply for the purpose of removing the rock which has already been disturbed and is lying loose on the bottom, and is, I am told, an obstruction to navigation. I cannot say that I see any particular advantage myself in having the work continued, since the canal will afford all the navigation that is necessary. As the hon. gentleman has mentioned the matter, it would be well to have it looked into fully before asking for any further appropriation. This is one of the works that the superintending engineer recommends very strongly.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Is this work paid for by the day or according to the quantities ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: It is on the basis of the agreement which was in force when I came into the department.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I would like the minister to ask the superintending engineer to give me a list of the steamers which use that channel, and I would like to know the name of any insurance company which will take a risk on steamers that will go down that channel. I intend taking this matter up again next session, and I would like to have the names of any good reliable vessel men who will agree to take any steamer drawing 14 feet of water down that channel. As to the agreement, these people had a contract for so many yards of excavation at $8.40 per yard, and I think it was the minister himself wTho changed that agreement to $425 per day. That plant Is standing there and we are paying $425 per day for nothing.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: My chief engineer says that the price and everything else was settled before I came to the department.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: The Minister of Railway* has a very short memory.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Is the hon. gentleman very proud of his ?
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
Yes, I have a good memory, and I know that there was a contract under which these parties claimed a certain amount from the late government.
I ordered the contract to cease and refused to pay, and gave them their remedy in the Exchequer Court. The hon. gentleman has asserted again and again that he is only continuing the contract which was made by the late government, and I have again and again pointed out the absurdity of his contention. These gentlemen had a contract per yard for excavation, and in order to find out whether the excavation was done to the proper depth or not, they had Mr. Kennedy, the engineer of the Harbour Commissioners at Montreal, up for the purpose of making an examination. I objected to paying the sum they claimed, because I looked upon it as one of the biggest frauds ever perpetrated by any firm on a government. It is utterly absurd to keep these dredges employed doing work which is entirely useless, and pay them besides this exorbitant price per day which my hon. friend from Grenville mentioned. Look at the enormous sums we have paid these contractors, nearly $1,000,000, and we have the same excuses offered every year. Last year the hon. minister told us that not only were they clearing out stones in the channel, but they had taken a contract to deepen it one foot more. Every year we have the same excuse, and every year we are told by the hon. gentleman that be is simply continuing the contract which his predecessors made. Even if that were true, that is no justification whatever. The engineers of his department might tell him that the work is entirely useless. As my hon. friend from Grenville say-s, the vessels that navigate the ordinary depth of the canal never use it at all, but utilize the canal altogether, and it is only light crafts that go down. Very seldom does a boat go down this channel, and yet these parties are year after year continuing this contract and being paid large amounts. I see that in the supplementary estimates he is asking $50,000 for work that was done last year in excess of the vote, parliament gave.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I did not get any vote last year at all.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Then the hon. gentleman must have been carrying on this work without any vote or authority. Is the $293,000 for the enlargement of the Gallops canal principally 1

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Yes.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: The minister says he had no vote last year, yet he proposes to spend to the 1st of June next, $50,000, for which he is asking a vote in the supplementary estimates.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
Does the hon. gentleman propose to continue this way ? If

the statements be correct, this expenditure is a burning scandal.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: The great trouble now is that if they do dredge out any more there, no matter how small, they will be drawing the water away over to that island and across the rapids and really interfering with the entrance of the present canal. If that water is to be drawn off by this dredge, something wifi have to be done. Since the minister has had charge of the department, $240,377 have been paid this firm, according to the Auditor General's Report, and then there is this $50,000 more, making a total of about $300,000. Previous to that there was $1,000,000 sunk right in that rapids, simply thrown away entirely.. I am quite satisfied that the minister cannot produce a man in his department, other than Mr. Rubidge, who will say that that channel is of any us% I am quite satisfied that if the chief engineer were put under oath, he would have to admit that the channel would be of no use at all. Why it should be continued, I cannot understand.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
It does seem rather an extraordinary condition of affairs that this dredge is employed at $425 a day to do work, according to the statement of my hon. friend, which is not only of no value to the country, but is actually a detriment, as it draws water from the mouth of the canal and makes it more difficult for vessels to get through. I do not suppose that any of the small craft that go down the rapids would have any difficulty in getting through the canal, and yet the minister expended $50,000 last year without a vote, in doing this work that is of no advantage at all.
I notice that in the supplementary estimates the hon. gentleman has $50,000 for deepening and widening these rapids. I suppose that this is to pay for the work for which a vote should have been taken last year, and which the hon. minister says is not yet paid for. I may be wrong in my understanding of what the hon. gentleman said, but if my construction is the correct one it seems an extraordinary way to administer the department. He proceeds with this work at $425 a day, and then asks for a vote of about $50,000, and that for work which my hon. friend says is useless.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: These small craft I may mention, never use this channel, but go down the regular steamboat channel on the other side, which has been used for forty years, because it is a very difficult matter to get into the channel. I do not believe that any large steamer can get through it. I remember the first trial made by a steamef to get through. She was one of the old Welland Canal steamers. Owing to the way the current runs she turned around and went backwards. After that, there were one or two small propellors tried it, but they tried it only once.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Do not the Richelieu steamers go through V
speakername: The MINISTER OK RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Not one goes down that channel. They come up that channel, as they always did. The hon. gentleman knows there is not one of the Richelieu steamers running the St. Lawrence that draws more than seven feet, and that 25 years ago there was nine feet of water there. The Richelieu steamers went tip the identical channel thirty years ago. So. the fact of deepening that channel is no help to them at all. Ever since this new lock has been there they go into the lock on the way upwards. But on the downward trip they go along the old channel they have been using for 25 or 30 years. I was speaking with the gentleman who has charge of the Woolvin fleet. They have chartered 20 steamers, the first of which is to sail from Duluth on the 5th of May.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: What capacity are they?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Sixty thousand bushels. But there is not one of these steamers that the insurance people will allow to go through that channel. And I am satisfied that next session the minister will i'Ot be able to stand up in this House and say that one single steamer of the Woolvin people's fleet has gone down through that channel. The lockmaster in charge of the lock right opposite can give the names of all the steamers that have used that channel this year. If the hon. minister next session can name one steamer of the size of those of the Woolvin fleet-and this was supposed to be made for vessels similar to those of that fleet-that goes down that channel and gets through safe, I will not say a word further, and he can go on paying these people $100,000 a year as long us he is minister.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: They will draw fourteen feet, will they not ?
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
Yes, the channel was supposed to be fourteen feet safe. It was made seventeen teet so that a vessel drawing fourteen feet would go through safe. Though it was seventeen feet, and they were paid in full for the seventeen feet, they were paid one hundred or two hundred thousand extra to make it one foot deeper, so that there might be no possible danger to vessels drawing fourteen feet. But will the hon. minister have a vessel sent down drawing fourteen feet, arid assume the responsibility of accident, instead of asking the companies to do so ? I feel quite justified in laying this matter before the minister and trying to get the expenditure stopped. This is not the first appeal I have made, for I have spoken of the matter year after year. If the minister wishes to continue the contract I will

have to continue making this appeal every year to try to get the matter straightened out, so that this .$100,000 a year may not continue to be divided among a few people, with profits of about $80,000. If it is to go on, I would rather have it put in straight as a charitable grant than to have it the way it is.
Mr. SPROUT,E.	What explanation has
the minister to give for the expenditure of this money without a vote of parliament ? And how does he manage to satisfy the Auditor General ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Last year when the question came up as to whether or not I should ask for an appropriation for this work, in view of what had taken place in parliament and the strong opinions that had been expressed by hon. gentlemen on both sides of the House about it, I declined to ask for any appropriation. I understand from the chief engineer that he informed Mr Gilbert that there was no appropriation and that the work could not be continued. There is no appropriation in the main estimates, as hon. gentlemen can see, nor is there art appropriation for next year. But there will be found, as inis beeu said, an appropriation of a small amount in the supplementary estimates for the current year. The appropriation. I am advised by the chief engineer, is necessary-not for the purpose of continuing the work, I do not propose to ask parliament for any money beyond this, a part of which is needed to pay the drawback. There is the amount of the drawback which we have to pay out of that $50,000. Then, I understood from the chief engineer that some rock had to be excavated which had been carried down into tlie channel, and which would impede navigation, and perhaps cause injury to vessels using the channel; and I have asked in the sup-plementarles for a small sum in addition to the drawback in order to cleir this out. so that there would 1>5 no ground for a claim for damages. There is nothing in tire estimates inserted with any intention to continue this expenditure or to continue this work. Mr. Rubidge and his assistant engineers are all strongly /if opinion that this is a very useful work. Thev do not agree with my hon. friend. But I do not propose to take the responsibility of continuing this work this year, and have nothing in the estimates for that purpose.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Has this company been going on earning money during the year, or are they putting in a claim for money earned which was not voted, and after being notified by the minister that he does not intend to continue the work ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: If they have done anything they have done it without any authority. My decision was last year not to proceed with
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: the work. The chief engineer was advised of that, and he notified the contractors that there was no appropriation for the purpose and therefore the work would not be continued. If they have gone and done any work they certainly had no authority, and it would be against my view that they should go on with the work of last summer.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Are there any claims put in ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Tiie chief engineer said they did some work without his knowledge.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: This firm started work a year ago this spring and they worked until file close of navigation, up to December, 1901. Therefore I can hardly believe they were working there for fun. I think they were getting $425 a day, at least they will put in a claim for tlfat amount. For that reason I was under the impression that they had been authorized to do it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: The chief engineer says he gave them no authority to do it.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Well, they were working there right along. Were they only paid up to the expiration of that vote ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: That is all.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Then they worked on afterwards and got nothing for it. Have they put in any claim for it ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: They certainly have got nothing.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Well, have they put in any claim for work up to December ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: The chief engineer says that he has received uo claim from them, though they have asked for an estimate.
speakername: Tlie MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: The government engineer that was in charge of that work remained there until December, lived right there on the boat, I know, until navigation closed.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: The chief engineer advises me that he does not know that to be a fact, and that if these people did work, they did it at their own risk without any authority from him, and they certainly had no authority from me.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
I may say for tlie benefit of tlie minister that the story of the rocks washing in there is the same old story we have been told year after year.
I understand that this story has impressed him with the need of going ahead. But I cannot see where the rocks come from that were washed into this channel. Tne bed of tlie river is flat above and I cannot see

where the rocks can come from. But that excuse has been given year after year to the minister in order that they may go on with this work. If the minister will take any thorough marine man and send him there, I am satisfied he will report that the channel is not navigable for any large steamer. Why cannot the minister simply wind up the work. I am afraid-because it is not the first time we have heard this story, not only from the minister but from others, that it would be ended up-I am afraid that next session I will come here and be told the same old story. Could the minister tell us now . if that work is to be continued ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I think I have come pretty near making that statement. I do not want to commit myself too" positively as to the future without hearing all that is to be said and considering it. But I have certainly decided not to ask for any appropriation for next year, I decided last year not to ask for any appropriation for this year, and I have put in that item of $50,000, and am advised that one-half of it at least is a drawback that has to be paid.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Why is your engineer attending to the work if you are not going on with it, and who gives a certificate for the progress estimates ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: The chief engineer says there has been no progress estimate^ sent in at all. I presume these people have been putting in their time and hope perhaps to get something. But they have made no claim, or intimated in any way to the department that they intend to make a claim.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: It seems to me to indicate very peculiar ideas as to the business methods of the department.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
Well, they have had a long number of years in which to form a judgment on the question.
Mr. BORDlON (Halifax). I do not sec that there is any particular need of a vote of parliament if they go on in this way from year to year. I do not quite understand the procedure. Is the engineer who is supposed to have been in charge of the work during the past season an officer of the government, and if so, has he been paid by the government for his work during the past: year V
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: We have an engineer-I understand his name is Ross-in charge of the canal. It may be, as the hon. member for Grenville (Mr. Reid) has said, that he was not paid at the time. I do not know about that.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
If this engineer, who is acting for the government, has been
superintending the work which these men have been doing without any appropriation apparently and apparently without any instructions, the government will be in rather an awkward position when the question of liability is raised. If the government's officer has been superintending the work which these men have been doing at the rate of $425 a day during the past season the government may have incurred liability, and, it may be that an appropriation of parliament would be needed, but it is certainly a very undesirable way of doing business. No appropriation was asked by the minister last year for the reason that he had not concluded to go on with the work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: 1 had concluded not to go on with the work.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: What is the name of the firm that is doing the work now ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: The Gilbert Dredging Conixiany.
speakername: The MINISTER. OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: What are the names of the gentlemen who control the firm ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: The two Gilbert Brothers. That is all the chief engineer knows and I do not know any more.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I think these are the only two.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Is it perfectly clear that no portion of the vote which is now asked is to be applied or can be applied for the purpose of paying for this unauthorized work ? This is not enlargement.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: This is for the Galops canal.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: And it does not touch this subject at all ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: No. During the time that the work has been going on the appropriation has always been under the heading of ' Galops Rapids.' That is the way it is entered in the supplementary estimates.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: It would seem that the Gilbert Brothers were working from the 1st of July, until the 1st of December, at a cost of about $12,000 a month, without any understanding with the department. As the hon. leader of the opposition (Mr. Borden, Halifax), has pointed out the hon. gentleman can hardly hope to escape responsibility. These people have their plant, they have been engaged by the department, under the engineer or some officer of the department. He has been on this pdant or on some part of It and he remained in possession of that work for five months. They incurred a liability of $60,000, and the hon. minister comes down now and does not ask the House for anything to provide for payment. The hon. minister cannot hope that these people will consent to go without their pay. The hon. minister proposes apparently to deal with these Gilbert Brothers in the same kindly manner in which he dealt with them before. I remember last year that a claim came up for $25,000 which Gilbert Brothers had made against the department. They put in a claim for $25,000 for extras done several years before the hon. minister came into the department. That claim the then hon. Minister of Railways and Canals (Mr. Haggart)

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: This is very interesting of course, but we might read it all over some Sunday when we have nothing else to do. I can put my hon. friend (Mr. Bennett) upon the right track if he will allow me. The Gilbert Brothers who preferred that claim which he has in contemplation are not the same Gilberts, so I am told by the engineer, and I believe that to be the case. There are five brothers and they afe not by any means associated together in business.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Then, it only shows how very pernicious the example of the hon. minister was. Here are two men named Gilbert, who had this claim against the department when the hon. member for Lanark (Mr. Haggart) was at the head of the department. He offered them a fiat to go into the courts* and prosecute that claim and they refused to go into the courts with it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
What is the use of my hon. friend starting at one o'clock in the morning upon a controversial question which he knows is not one-sided, which he knows has another side and which he knows has been debated in parliament two or three times and which might be debated again if it were a little earlier in the session and
Mr. BORDEN (Halifax)
a little earlier in the evening. I would be pleased to hear the hon. gentleman repeat the speech he made on a previous occasion, but I appeal to him whether it is not a little late to revive that subject.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I was starting out to say that the hon. minister by his kindness to these Gilbert Brothers, seems in that particular case to have inoculated the whole family of Gilberts with the result that we must pay this $60,000, and the hon. minister cannot shelter himself behind the statement that he has made because these men certainly went on with the work and he did not stop them.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
If the hon. minister will look at his report for the last year he will see that .Mr. Rubidge says :
Operations on north and island shoals were resumed ir. May and June, 1901, will be continued until the close of the season.
And they were. The appropriation for the Galops rapids runs to June 30, 1901, at which time notice was given to the contractors. I will admit that according to his statement Mr. Rubidge gave notice to the contractors, but on the 1st of May, when Mr. Rubidge had that dredge at work on these rapids, he placed Mr. Ross and a staff of engineers In charge of the work. They were not in charge of the canal, they were in charge of the work and that stall' of engineers, notwithstanding the fact that lie notified them that the vote had lapsed, reniained on these vessels until the snow made them stop in the fall. They were not taken off the work but the work went right along.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: And the government engineers were right there.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Mr. Ross has another position on the Grenville canal. When the hon. minister states that Mr. Ross was in charge of the canal I understand that once a month he took the pay cheques down and paid the men, but he was in charge of the work, and I know the names of other assistants that were with him. If they had stopped the work on the 1st of July then, of course, no fault would be found. I am making this appeal to try and get this straightened out so that it will not be continued.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Did the engineer send in no report in regard to the work that had been done during the summer ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: They seem to have had a pleasant little time amongst themselves; these gentlemen with the dredge at $425 a day, and the engineer and his staff enjoying themselves without sending in any 'report. They apparently have expended nearly enough to enable Captain Bernier to discover the north pole, and all that lias been done without the knowledge of the minister.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
I make no claim to omniscience or to omnipresence, and I certainly could not be supposed to know that the men were going on to prosecute a work that we had decided we would not continue and for which we obtained no appropriation.
Mr. -BENNETT. There were no applications made by these people from the 1st of July, to the 1st of December, for remuneration ?
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: None whatever.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: What was the date of the first application ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Not until within a month of this date. The chief engineer tells me they came up about a month ago to ask whether or not there -would be any appropriation in he estimates next year for the carrying out of the work.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: What was the amount of the claim 1

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: There was no amount stated.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: It seems incredible. These men were paid for a time up to the 1st of July, on monthly estimates I suppose, but then they continued, under the supervision of the government engineer, doing work from the 1st of July, to the close of navigation they never made a claim for it until a month ago when they came to the department and incidentally mentioned this trifling amount of $60,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I am informed by the chief engineer that they stated no amount. The only amount mentioned was that one mentioned by the superintending engineer.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: When did Mr. Rubidge make this report ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: When he was asked for his report in view of the preparation of the estimates.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: When Mr. Rubidge was notified by the department that the vote had lapsed was it not his duty to take his staff off ? Did he inform the department that these people were persisting in the work ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: As far as I can see now. I would like to hear what Mr. Rubidge has to say in his own defence. It seems to me that was his duty.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I should think he would be entitled to censure for not doing that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
I should think so.
North channel-forming dam, $56,250.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: This is simply throwing this money away. You had better throw the money into the river than put that dam across there. This is a scheme put up by the Gilberts to get work for $56,000. There is no question about that. I would really like to know what this dam is going to be.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: The Gilberts have nothing to do with this. Cleveland is the contractor.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Is the dam put there for the purpose of improving this channel that we have been discussing ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: The report is that there are cross currents.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: This channel that the Gilberts have been working at for the last twenty-five years

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Oh.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: They commenced the channel in 1876 and they have been working continuously ever since. This water that comes between these two islands runs directly across the channel the Gilberts have been working at, and this dam is simply put there to stop that current. Really and truly if the minister looks into it, he will see that it is of no earthly use whatever. I appeal to him not to put a dam there, because it would injure the rapids, and I believe that the vesselmen will condemn it. It would be far better to give whoever the contractor is, half the amount he would make in profit and not have the dam there at all. I appeal to the minister that that dam should not be put there.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I will tell the hon. gentleman what I will do. I will undertake that the money will not be expended until I have the subject thoroughly investigated, and until I have had the opinion of other engineers. Not being an engineer myself, I cannot form judgment upon a question of this kind. I can, however, probably decide not to spend, and I will not do so until I ascertain from independent engineers that it would be a proper expenditure to make. Of course, my hon. friend knows that there is always a great difference of opinion with regard to the navigation of channels.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
I can quite understand that, and the answer of the hon. minister is quite fair ; but large vessels will never go through these rapids, and this is a part of that other scheme. If the hon. minister will look into the matter, I feel satisfied that he will never spend the money.
The MINISTER OF RAILWA18 AND CANALS. I have already mentioned that this is a continuation of work that has already been started in the same direction.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: That other work of Mr. Cleveland's is satisfactory, and he is doing his work very well. But it is not part of Mr. Cleveland's original contract.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: The building of the dam will not absorb the whole of this money.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Yes, it will, because it is in a bad place and is a very large dam. It is a mile and a half from Mr. Cleveland's original contract.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: I would not like to undertake to say that no part of this money will be expended, because it may be necessary to spend a portion of it for the purpose of. completing the channel which I spoke of, and which the hon. gentleman says is a very proper work to do ; but I will undertake to say as to the dam, to which he takes exception, that nothing will be expended until inquiry is made.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Any money voted for Mr. Cleveland's contract is perfectly right.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Do I understand that this vote is not for any part of the Gilbert work at all ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: It has no connection at all with their work.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Does the hon. gentleman not think that we have gone far enough to-night ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: If the hon. gentlemen opposite will consent to the rest of the items of my department going through to-night, I shall be willing to discuss any of these items on the supplementary canal votes.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: There are a couple of members of the House who want to speak on the Trent canal.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
I will say the same with regard to them.
To repair locks one and two Lachine canals, $100,000. '
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Why spend such a large sum on the old locks ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext:
They are in a very insufficient condition and we have to repair them.
Some resolutions reported.
On motion of the Minister of Finance the House adjourned at 1.30 a.m. Friday.
speakername: The MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND CANALS.

maintopic: SUPPLY-THE SEARCH FOR THE NORTH POLE.
speechtext: Friday, May 2, 1902.
